title: Implement retention-signal propagation for aggregated usage probes and consent-scoped exports
creator: Riley Chen
description: Background: Console telemetry currently stores aggregated usage probes (route hit counts, latency histograms, feature-flag events) without a consistent, queryable retention signal tied to user consent or legal holds. This creates gaps when customers request data deletion or when consent state changes — aggregated buckets may still contain identifiable or regulated derivatives. Goal: implement a retention-signal propagation layer that tags, stores, and enforces retention metadata for aggregated probes and consent-scoped exports so that downstream queries and exports can respect deletion/consent windows without requiring full re-aggregation.
design_summary: 1) Introduce a small immutable metadata envelope for each aggregated probe shard containing: original time window, contributing partition keys, retention_ttl_bucket (enum), consent_version_id, and optional legal_hold_id. 2) Store envelopes alongside aggregated metrics in the analytics store (S3 Parquet partition + Dynamo index) so deletion workflows can mark envelopes as expired instead of materialized value rewrites. 3) Implement query-time gating layer in the analytics query API that filters aggregates whose envelopes are expired or under legal hold, with the option to return a masked/partial response (e.g., drop low-count buckets). 4) Extend existing deletion orchestrator to propagate consent version changes to envelopes and schedule tombstone manifests for downstream exporters and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregated probe writes include retention metadata envelope and pass schema validation
Query API filters expired/held envelopes and returns masked aggregates per policy
Deletion orchestrator updates envelopes for consent revocations within SLA (< 2 hours) and creates tombstone manifests
End-to-end test demonstrating consent revocation removes user-associated probe contribution from exported CSV
Load tests show <5% tail-latency increase on analytics queries after gating layer added
tasks: Schema change: add retention_envelope to aggregated probe Parquet (data infra)
Write path: enrich shard writer to emit envelopes and index keys
Query layer: implement gating and masking logic with feature flags
Orchestrator: consent propagation hook and tombstone manifest generator
Consumer update: CSV export pipeline respects tombstone manifests
Confluence doc + runbook for on-call (how to remediate stuck envelopes)
